sections.h2: Apparel is about 43% of India's textile and apparel exports, led by woven Chapter 62

sections.means: Apparel is the single largest textile and apparel category, and it is built on cotton-skewed woven and knitted lines.

sections.h2: Cotton textiles hold a larger export share than man-made textiles, about 33% to 15%

chart.title: Cotton textiles hold a larger export share than man-made textiles in Apr–Oct FY25
chart.sub: Share of the export basket, %, Apr–Oct FY25.
chart.source: DGCI&S, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Cotton textiles were ~33% of the Apr–Oct FY25 export basket against ~15% for man-made textiles, even though man-made fibres are about 70% of fibre consumption.
sections.todo: Track the synthetic-fibre lines the post lists, such as 610323, 610333 and 610343, as the place where India's cotton skew shows up.

sections.h2: Technical textiles are 12–15% of India's value chain, against ~50% in advanced economies

chart.title: Technical textiles are 12–15% of India's value chain against ~50% in advanced economies
chart.sub: Technical textiles as a share of the textile value chain, %.

sections.means: India holds only 4–5% of the global technical-textiles market, and the post ties the gap to specialty fibres and technology it must import.
sections.todo: Judge the NTTM and PLI schemes by whether they close the specialty-fibre import gap in the high-value segments.
